podcast.title: Equipment Sales Spike
podcast.body: The rise of E-Lectronica led to a spike in sales of turntables, CD decks, and mixers, indicating a growing interest in DJ culture, while guitar sales simultaneously fell. "It seemed that everybody wanted to be a DJ. Sales of turntables and CD decks and mixers spiked guitar sales fell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Genre Inclusivity (Late 90s)
podcast.body: At the end of the 1990s, the term E-Lectronica encompassed a wide array of subgenres, including techno, deep house, electronic dance, and ambient, offering music for both dancing and relaxation. "Again, this is what we called EDM back at the end of the 90s. It was a term that encompassed everything from techno to deep house, from electronic dance to ambient. You could dance to it, or just chill."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Late 1990s Explosion
podcast.body: Around 1999, E-Lectronica, then known as what is now called EDM, experienced a significant explosion in popularity, with acts like The Prodigy and The Chemical Brothers selling "boatloads of albums." "Electronic music was also exploding. What we call EDM today was known as E-Lectronica in most circles back in 1999, acts like the prodigy and the chemical brothers and aethics when we're selling boatloads of albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Mainstream Penetration
podcast.body: Electronic sounds began to infiltrate various forms of media, including movies, TV shows, and TV commercials, and were extensively explored by video game composers, leading to a rapid evolution into subgenres like jungle, drum and bass, and electro-clash. "Electronic sounds started seeping into movies, and TV, and TV commercials. Composers of music for video games went deep into the genre. And things evolved very quickly."
